title: Heterogeneously Integrated Squeezed-Light Generation and Detection on a Single Photonic Chip
authors: Haoran Chen, Benjamin Westcott, Fatemehsadat Tabatabaei, Xiangwen Guo, Shuman Sun, Zijiao Yang, Gedalia Y. Koehler, Beichen Wang, Shadrach Sarpong, Steven Bowers, Olivier Pfister, Andreas Beling, Xu Yi
abstract: Squeezed light underpins quantum-enhanced sensing and continuous-variable quantum information processing, and integrated photonics offers a route to producing it at scale. Universal to these applications are squeezed-light generation and measurement. Importantly, quantum measurements serve not only as readout but also as active operations in quantum-state evolution. However, integrating squeezed-light generation and photodetection on the same photonic chip has remained challenging because they impose fundamentally conflicting material requirements: low optical loss to preserve quantum correlations, but efficient photon absorption for photodetection. Here, we demonstrate squeezed-light generation, routing, and balanced homodyne detection integrated on a single photonic chip through heterogeneous integration. A two-mode squeezed quantum microcomb comprising 34 quantum modes is measured with approximately 3 dB squeezing. Our work establishes a scalable architecture for fully integrated squeezed-light quantum photonic systems, unifying quantum-state generation, processing, and detection on a single chip.
summary: The research presents an experimental demonstration of integrating squeezed-light generation and detection onto one photonic chip using heterogeneous integration. By overcoming material conflicts between low-loss transmission and high-absorption detection, the authors achieved 3 dB squeezing with a high total quantum efficiency. This establishes a scalable platform for advanced quantum photonic applications.
main_problem: Integrating squeezed-light generation and photodetection on a single photonic chip is challenging due to conflicting material requirements: low loss for quantum correlations versus efficient absorption for detection.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated a scalable architecture by integrating all three stages (generation, routing, and detection) on one chip, achieving measurable 3 dB squeezing with low overall circuit loss.
method: They used heterogeneous integration to combine components like Kerr microcavities for squeezing, tunable filters for routing, and modified uni-traveling carrier photodiodes for balanced homodyne detection.
model_or_system: The system is a single photonic chip built on SiN, incorporating an Optical Parametric Oscillator (OPO) pumped by a continuous wave laser to generate two-mode squeezed light. Detection relies on heterogeneously integrated MUTC photodiodes.
key_observables: Squeezing level ($\approx 3 	ext{ dB}$), total quantum efficiency ($72\%$), and quadrature noise variances relative to shot noise.
important_parameters: Total optical loss of $1.1 	ext{ dB}$ post-squeezer, pump power near OPO threshold, and the measured MMI splitting ratio ($46/54$ vs designed).
main_assumptions: The primary limitation noted is that squeezing level is limited by component non-idealities like squeezer escape efficiency and residual loss.
figures_summary: Figures show architectural diagrams, sideviews of photodiodes, characterization spectra (transmission/mode), noise spectrum validation confirming sub-shot-noise operation, and total quantum efficiency measurements.
paper_structure: The paper details the architecture, presents component characterizations (loss, QE), demonstrates the measurement of quadrature noise variances to quantify squeezing below the shot noise limit, and discusses the scalability of the integrated platform.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses hardware bottlenecks in quantum optics by demonstrating a fully integrated platform for continuous-variable quantum state generation and measurement, which is crucial for scalable quantum networking and computation.

figures.caption: FIG. 1: Architecture and building blocks of the heterogeneous integrated squeezed-light generation and detection on a photonic chip. (a) Illustration of the heterogeneous quantum photonic integrated circuit. The quantum light source is a squeezed quantum microcomb generated in a SiN optical microcavity through Kerr nonlinearity. The squeezer is followed by a tunable ring filter to route the odd-number quantum modes (qumodes) to the balanced homodyne detection (BHD). The routed odd number qumodes are then combined with local os- cillator on a 50/50 multimode interferometry (MMI) coupler, and detected on a pair of balanced MUTC photo- diodes heterogeneously integrated on the SiN QPIC. FIG. 3: Experimental setup and squeezing measurement. (a) Experimental setup. The pump laser and the local oscillators are created off-chip and coupled into the squeezed light chip through lens fiber array. The bichro- matic LOs are created using electro-optics modulation and a line-by-line programmable waveshaper (WS) filter. A probe laser is coupled into the chip from the opposite direction to monitor the frequency alignment of the squeezer and the tunable filter. A low bandwidth DC probe is used to control the integrated heater on the ring filter, and an RF probe is used to bias the integrated photodiodes and read-out the photocurrents. (a) Quadrature noise variances (blue) relative to shot noise (red) of odd number qumodes from (-7,7) to (-37,37). The qumodes measured are marked by the red arrows.
